clause_evidence.reasoning: Nine samples directly assess reading fractions by asking students to identify the word name for given symbolic fractions. Reading is demonstrated through questions asking how fractions are read in words and which word names represent given fractions, providing comprehensive support for the reading requirement.

Eleven samples directly assess writing fractions by asking students to convert verbal descriptions into fraction notation. These items consistently request symbolic representation given in English words, demonstrating comprehensive support for the writing requirement across multiple denominators.

While the packet includes various fractions with different denominators and numerators, no sample assesses whether students understand the mathematical concept of similar or equivalent fractions. Although 2/4 appears once, it is never compared to 1/2 or other equivalent forms. No item asks students to identify which fractions are similar or recognize equivalent fractions, representing a significant gap in assessing understanding of what makes fractions similar.

All twenty samples exclusively use standard fraction notation, presenting fractions in numerator over denominator format. The notation is consistent throughout, and students engage with it in both reading and writing contexts, demonstrating that this requirement is fully met.
